name: Search field
summary: Lets people type what they are looking for.
description: A search field collects a search term: a query for a whole site, a filter for a list. It is a Text field with a search glyph at its start, exposed to assistive technology as a search box, and whose clear control the platform provides. It has a visible label, which may be the only word next to it (Search), and an optional description; it has no error state: a search that finds nothing is reported by the results, not by the field.

anatomy.description: Root. Stacks the label, the control, the description and the error message; carries the size and the forced state.
Text naming the field. Provides the accessible name; activating it focuses the control.
Box holding the control and the search glyph drawn over its start edge.
The editable box: the native search input, drawn by the component with the search glyph over its start edge. Receives focus, holds the term and shows the placeholder while empty.
Search glyph of the icon font at the start of the control, saying what the field is for. Hidden from assistive technology, which learns it from the role.
Optional help text under the control (format, example, consequence), associated with it as its description.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Control height, inline padding and text size scale together; label, description and error keep their size.

options.description: Dense forms, toolbars, table rows (32 px high).
Prominent, single fields: a search page, a sign-in form (48 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What the field asks for, as a noun phrase (Email address). Always visible.

properties.name: Placeholder
properties.description: Short hint shown while the field is empty (what can be searched: Search projects). Never the label.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text: expected format, example, or what the value is used for.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: The field must be filled to submit the form.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Non-interactive and skipped by the keyboard; the value stays visible. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

states.description: Resting: an outlined box on the default surface.
Pointer over the control. The box takes the surface hover tint; the border does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Focus on the control, from the keyboard or a pointer: an editable field shows the shared focus ring outside its border however it was focused.
Non-interactive. Box, value, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors; hover and focus do not apply.

notes: Label, control, description and error message stack, separated by container.gap; the control fills the width of the component, which the layout sizes.
Inline padding, minimum height and text size come from the size option; the corner radius and the border width do not change.
The search glyph sits over the start edge of the control, which reserves room for it with padding-inline-start.

name.text: Computed from the label, associated with the control as its label element on the web. The description is exposed as the accessible description; the placeholder is exposed as a placeholder, not as the name.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the control. A disabled control is not focusable and is skipped.
In browsers that provide a clear control, clears the term.

guidelines.text: Expose the searchbox role, the name, the value and the disabled state through the platform's native search control, so assistive technology announces it as a search field.

Use the native input type=search without a list attribute: it exposes the searchbox role and may take the platform's look and clear control. The clear control is the browser's: the component neither styles nor removes it.
Every search field has a visible label associated with the control programmatically, even when it is just Search; the glyph alone is not a label.
Associate the label with a label element whose for attribute names the control's id, and the description with aria-describedby.
The placeholder is a short hint of what can be searched, never the label: it disappears as soon as people type, and is not exposed as the name when a label exists.
The search glyph is decorative and hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden="true": an icon-font glyph is written as its ligature name, which would otherwise be read with the value.

Label, value and description contrast at least 4.5:1 with their background in every color mode and enabled state: label and value 19.07:1 (light) and 11.27:1 (dark) on the default surface, description 12.87:1 and 8.80:1, placeholder 6.08:1 and 6.36:1. The glyph is decoration and needs no contrast of its own (6.08:1 and 6.36:1 anyway). Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

The border is what identifies the field, so it contrasts at least 3:1 with the adjacent surface in every color mode: 12.87:1 (light) and 8.80:1 (dark) on the default surface at rest, 12.14:1 and 8.06:1 on the hover tint; the focus ring 5.79:1 and 12.80:1. Disabled is exempt.
A visible focus indicator appears when the control receives focus, drawn outside its border.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, which browsers match whenever an editable field has focus, pointer or keyboard.
Every size is a pointer target of at least 24 x 24 CSS pixels through its minimum height: 32, 40 and 48 pixels.
A disabled field leaves the focus order.

A search field is an editable text field that displays a search icon, a clear button and placeholder text; use placeholder text to help people know what they can search for. The small and medium sizes (32 and 40 pt) fall under the 44 x 44 pt hit region on iOS today.
Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; the small and medium sizes (32 and 40 dp) fall under it on Android today.
Color transitions of the control are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

guidelines: The label says what is searched: Search, Search projects, Filter by name. Sentence case, no colon.
The placeholder gives an example of a query or the scope (Name, email or role), never the label.
A search field has no error message: an empty result is reported next to the results, with what to try next.

examples.name: Medium, with a value and description

decisions.text: The control follows the Text field's colors: a box on the default surface outlined in the accent neutral border color; hover tints it with the surface hover color and keeps the border; disabled takes the shared disabled colors. Value text is primary, the placeholder tertiary, the description secondary, the glyph the tertiary icon color.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library maps no color to form controls. The accent neutral border is the lightest neutral border that keeps 3:1 against the surface in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11); the hover tint reuses the surface's own hover step.

decisions.text: Three sizes from the Figma library's space and body scales: small (32 px high, 8 px inline padding, 14 px text), medium (40, 12, 16, the default) and large (48, 16, 20); the border is 0.6 px (stroke-width.sm) and the corners 4 px (corner-radius.xs) at every size; label, description and error message keep 14 px.

A search glyph (the icon font) sits over the start edge of the control at 16, 20 or 24 px by size, 8 px from the edge; the control reserves 28, 36 or 40 px of start padding for it. It is hidden from assistive technology; the role says what the field is for.
A search field has no invalid or read-only state and no error message: an empty result is reported by the results. The clear control is the browser's.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions field-colors, sizes, search-glyph, no-error-state). Native search input in a wrapper with a label element, a search glyph and a description; states default, hover, focus-visible, disabled; sizes small, medium, large. Contrast on the default surface, light / dark: label and value 19.07 / 11.27, description 12.87 / 8.80, placeholder and glyph 6.08 / 6.36, border 12.87 / 8.80 (12.14 / 8.06 on hover), focus ring 5.79 / 12.80.
